Questions / Christian

How do I actually live like Jesus?

Here. With these people. With the power I have.

I’m building software, pursuing an account of the physical world, and trying to follow Christ. I want those commitments to answer to one another—in the way I work, listen and care.

Explore a situation in The Field →Follow the questions ↓

The question becomes real in what I do next.

An open hand. A real responsibility.

Faith has to meet the person in front of me.

I want following Christ to become visible in how I pay attention, share power and remain answerable. Sometimes that means helping. Sometimes it means a boundary that protects someone else.

01 / Attend

See the person.

Listen before I turn someone’s situation into my explanation. Separate what I know from what I am assuming.

02 / Make room

Keep a choice open.

Offer help without making submission its price. Accept a cost freely, and ask who else is being asked to carry it.

03 / Answer for it

Stay open to repair.

Give reasons. Hear an objection. Protect people from harm, and change course when the consequences call for it.

A Christian starting point: Philippians 2:3–8 · John 13:1–17 · Luke 10:25–37

Faith / physics / software / the work of care

Questions I have to answer.

If my tools, explanations and beliefs ask for trust, I owe people ways to question them. These are some of the places where that responsibility becomes concrete.

01 / Power & agency

Where am I helping—and where am I taking over?

Having the power to act does not settle what I owe the person in front of me. I need to ask whose freedom my help makes possible.

Explore power and agency →

02 / Engineering & restraint

What must I refuse, even if I can make it work?

A working system can still ask too much of people. I want my engineering to make its authority, limits and costs visible.

Examine permission and responsibility →

03 / Physics & truth

What would make me surrender the theory I want to be true?

If I ask an explanation to earn my trust, I have to leave it somewhere to fail. That includes the explanations I most want to succeed.

Enter the working laboratory →

04 / Sourcery & accountability

Can the software I build answer for what it does?

People should be able to follow a change, question its reasons and retain a meaningful say in what happens next.

Follow the human question in Sourcery →

05 / Attention & care

How do I keep caring when understanding isn’t enough?

I can understand a principle and still miss the person. I want to practise attention, listen to correction and keep finding contact.

Begin with care →

06 / History & repair

How do I repair harm without rewriting what happened?

An apology cannot make the past disappear. Repair has to leave room for truth, changed practice and the other person’s boundaries.

Follow the visible seam →

Where the question meets a situation

Someone asks for help. What do I owe them?

The Field begins with a workshop shift that needs covering. A private request. An uncertain reason. A problem that will still exist tomorrow.

I want to examine what a choice does now, what it teaches a relationship, and what it makes normal over time. You can bring a different judgment—and ask what the scenario leaves out.

Enter the workshop encounter →

One fictional encounter. Five choices. Room to disagree.

Explore a household over time →

Urgency without taking over

What is mine to do next?

I cannot wait until every explanation is complete to practise care. I can act with reasons, acknowledge what I don’t know, and remain responsible for repair.
